# CMF-true-stereo **Real left/right stereo on the CMF Phone 1.** The earpiece becomes the left speaker, the bottom speaker the right — no custom kernel, just root.

Download the module · Get the app · How stereo works

| | | |---|---| | 🔊 **Stereo** | Earpiece = left, speaker = right. Games, films and music finally have sides. | | 📢 **Mono** | Default. Both speakers play the full mix: louder and fuller than the bottom speaker alone. | | 📱 **App** | *CMF Stereo*, a clean Nothing-style app: on/off, Mono/Stereo, two 1–10 levels. | | 🛟 **Safe** | Patches nothing it has not verified, never touches the vendor partition, and undoes itself after two failed boots. | ### Install in three steps 1. Flash the zip in **Magisk / KernelSU / APatch** and reboot. 2. Open **CMF Stereo** and pick **Stereo**, or tap **Action** on the module's card in Magisk, or in a terminal: `su -c stereoctl channels stereo`. It switches at once (the sound stops for a moment; press play again). 3. Turn the phone sideways either way: left and right follow the screen. Works on the **CMF Phone 1 (A015)**. On any other phone it installs and does nothing. > **Before you use stereo** > - Stereo turns off Awinic's speaker protection for media (calls always keep > it). The module's own protection stands in: the speaker is held **6 dB > below the amp's full output** at its loudest (app speaker level 10, 2 dB > more per level down), its deepest bass is held back when it gets loud, and > the earpiece is kept from clipping. Use **Mono** for loud listening. > - If the phone fails to boot twice in a row with stereo on, the module > removes stereo on its own and falls back to Mono. > > Details in [Mono and stereo](#mono-and-stereo). ## Status **Current release: v1.0.6** (CMF Phone 1, Nothing OS B4.1, Android 16). Stereo works and is in daily use on the test phone, with the module's own protection running in the audio HAL (deep bass guard, earpiece limiter, optional speaker boost and earpiece leveller). Mono and Stereo switch without a reboot, and Magisk offers new releases as updates. Left and right follow the phone's orientation for every way apps play sound on this phone. "While playing" engages the earpiece for games and music alike. The full history of findings, tests and fixes is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). **Verified on the phone** - v1.0.5 earpiece leveller: a clear difference on the earpiece side, with no distortion heard. - Stereo: a left-only file plays on the earpiece only, the speaker's right slot silent, with Dirac on and off. Mono: both play the full mix. - Switching Mono and Stereo at once (audio HAL restart, no reboot) from `stereoctl channels`, both apps and Magisk's Action button; Magisk's Update button. - Left and right follow the rotation: ordinary apps and music players (USB Audio Player Pro, bit-perfect too), InShot, YouTube, games, VLC (its own audio effect: swapped by the HAL, v1.0.2), and the CMF L/R Test's MUSIC, MOVIE, MOVIE + EFFECT, GAME, SPEECH, AAUDIO, AAUDIO SHARED and FLOAT buttons. - "While playing" (v1.0.3): games (`dsp_fast`) and music players (`dsp_music`, `dsp_primary`) both engage the earpiece. - Protection (v1.0.4): `stereoctl protect` reports it running after the first sound, and every setting was tried and works (ceilings as designed, e.g. speaker level 5, bass strong: -4 dBFS on the signal, -20 dB below the amp's full output). - Earpiece at the receiver amp's top step (+8 dB); hi-res playback still works in stereo. **Not tested on a phone yet** - **v1.0.6** telling the apps: after a change made outside CMF Stereo (`stereoctl`, Magisk's Action button, the daemon's switch back to mono, and once when the daemon starts) the module asks each installed app to read the state again (`content call ... --method stateChanged`), so Nothing Settings' Stereo speakers page and Sound row follow at once. Tested here: both apps' providers called (a stand-in `content`), 198 checks in four shells. - Boost 6 over a longer listen (it was tried briefly with the other settings). - The protection after a live switch from a mono boot: by design it starts only after a reboot (the library is not in place until then; stereo plays as v1.0.3, boost ignored). - The safety nets that need a failure: the crash-loop guard (3 audio HAL restarts within a minute in stereo -> mono), the boot watchdog (two failed boots -> mono), a failed live switch ending on the stock files. Each is covered by the tests on fake files. - The next Nothing OS update: the guard that turns stereo off for an unknown build, and re-staging during a module update. - How the speaker holds up to long, loud stereo listening. **Pending** - After the next Nothing OS update: check the vendor file hashes and add the new build. - Earpiece leveller (optional, not built): raises the earpiece's quiet and medium passages, peaks never above today's, no frequency changed. - Known limit: an app with its own audio effect (VLC) and an ordinary app playing on the same output at once, earpiece on the right: one of them is reversed (the HAL sees only the mix). - Compressed offload: Android refuses it on this phone (Dirac is on for the output mix), so apps never use it here; not worth testing further. - A short clip of the two drivers splitting a game's or film's audio, for this page. **Fixed recently** - v1.0.4: in stereo the speaker got up to about 10 dB more deep bass than Awinic lets through in mono, and the earpiece clipped in its top 1.5 dB (CMF L/R Test DRIVER STUDY). The bass guard and the earpiece limiter hold both; a crash-loop guard puts the stock files back if the audio HAL keeps restarting in stereo. - v1.0.3: "While playing" watched only the DSP's music task, so games played on the speaker only. It now watches every playback task. - v1.0.2: VLC did not follow the rotation (Android leaves a track with its own audio effect unswapped); the HAL now swaps exactly those outputs. - Older: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). --- ## About A Magisk / KernelSU / APatch module that makes the **CMF Phone 1** play media out of its **earpiece as well as its bottom speaker** — in true stereo if you want it. It has two channel modes: - **mono** (default, stock audio): both drivers play the same full mix — louder, fuller and taller than the single bottom-firing speaker. This was the whole module once, back when it was called cmf-fake-stereo. - **stereo**: real left/right. The **earpiece plays the left channel and the speaker the right**. It costs Awinic's speaker-protection processing on media; the module's own protection (a fixed amp attenuation, a deep bass guard and an earpiece limiter, measured against what Awinic does) stands in. See [Mono and stereo](#mono-and-stereo). Getting stereo took finding the two places the phone folds the speaker to mono; the [Findings](#findings-what-this-device-actually-does) section shows the measurements rather than asking you to take my word. Verified on **A015 / Tetris, MT6878, Nothing OS B4.1, Android 16.** ## What it does - **Real stereo** in stereo mode: earpiece = left channel, bottom speaker = right - **Mono** mode: both speakers play the full mix, with full speaker protection - Plays media through the earpiece alongside the speaker, automatically - Earpiece at the receiver amp's maximum, +8 dB (`Handset Volume 0`), the same value the HAL uses - Applies only while audio is playing, so the receiver is not held energised - Steps aside for headphones and Bluetooth - Restores every control it touches on stop, disarm or uninstall - Disarms itself if it ever causes a failed boot - Switch modes with `stereoctl channels mono|stereo`, the app, or the Action button on the module's card in Magisk / KernelSU / APatch; the stereo overlay removes itself after two failed boots - Says on the module's card what is running: `[Stereo]`, `[Mono]`, `[Off]`, or `[Stereo unavailable]` after a Nothing OS update ## What it does not do - **No Awinic protection on media in stereo.** Awinic's DSP processing is the part that folds to mono, so stereo replaces it with the module's own, simpler protection (see [Mono and stereo](#mono-and-stereo)). Its model of the speaker, live from the amp's current and voltage sense, is not copied. - **No extra volume from the main speaker.** It is untouched. - **Nothing on other devices out of the box.** It installs inert elsewhere and ships a probe to work out that device's routing. ## Quick start Flash the zip (build it with `./build.sh`, or grab a release), reboot, play something. That is the whole setup on a CMF Phone 1 — the verified routing is preconfigured. To check it is working, with audio playing: ```sh su stereoctl status # all three controls should show want= matching now= stereoctl solo # speaker off, earpiece only - proves it is really the earpiece stereoctl unsolo ``` For real stereo (applied at once): ```sh su -c stereoctl channels stereo ``` If it is ever silent, `stereoctl doctor` walks every layer that can cause that and names the one responsible. ## On other devices It installs with an empty `actions.conf` and changes nothing. Run `stereoctl probe` to dump the audio hardware — ALSA topology, every mixer control, smart-amp drivers, HAL configs and MediaTek's AudioParam tree — then `stereoctl report` to fold it into one shareable text file. The routing for that device gets written into `actions.conf` from what the probe finds. See [Why it ships empty elsewhere](#why-it-ships-empty-elsewhere). --- ## How it works Three layers, smallest hammer first. **1. Mixer actions (`actions.conf`).** The real work. An ALSA mixer control somewhere enables the receiver output stage; on MediaTek there is usually also a routing control that decides which DL (downlink) stream feeds it. Setting those while the speaker is playing is what puts the earpiece to work next to the speaker. The audio HAL rewrites mixer controls on every route change, so a one-shot write does not survive the next stream start. A small daemon re-asserts the values every couple of seconds and — by default — only while audio is actually playing, so the earpiece is not left energised all day. Everything touched has its original value saved under `/data/adb/cmf-stereo/state/` and restored on stop, disarm or uninstall. **2. Audio policy overlay (`stereoctl xml-patch`, optional).** If the policy declares the speaker as `AUDIO_CHANNEL_OUT_MONO`, the framework downmixes to one channel before the HAL ever sees it, and no amount of mixer work brings the second channel back. The patch widens only the speaker `` to stereo, in an overlay copy — the vendor partition is never written. It is opt-in, validated before it is installed, and reversible. **3. What the CMF Phone 1 actually needed.** Worth recording, because it was not any of the obvious answers and the probe is what found it. Media on this device never touches the internal codec. Playback runs: ``` DL_24CH_CH1/CH2 ──▶ I2SOUT4_CH1/CH2 ──▶ Awinic aw_dev_0 smart PA ──▶ speaker ◀── I2SIN4 ──▶ UL3 (IV-sense feedback) ``` The earpiece hangs off the internal codec's DAC (`ADDA_DL`), and that DAC normally has **no source connected at all** — every one of its ~20 input switches sits Off. So pointing `RCV Mux` at the receiver routes it to a silent wire, which is exactly what happened on the first attempt. The switch that matters is `ADDA_DL_CH1 DL_24CH_CH1`: it feeds the internal DAC from the same `DL_24CH` stream already going to the speaker amp. Turn it on, then open `RCV Mux`, and the earpiece plays. There is only one Awinic device (`aw_dev_0`), so there is no second amp channel to press into service — the internal codec was the only way in. That alone gives both drivers the same full mix: **mono mode**. Real stereo needed one more step — switching off the two places the phone folds the speaker to mono — which is what `stereoctl channels stereo` adds (see [Findings](#findings-what-this-device-actually-does) and [Mono and stereo](#mono-and-stereo)). ## Findings: what this device actually does ### Where the speaker is folded to mono Earlier revisions of this section said both transducers were hard-wired to channel 1, then that a custom kernel would be needed, then that the DSP firmware was the limit. All three were wrong. Each stage was measured with a test file that has sound on the left channel only and silence on the right, by switching the amp to its right slot: silence there means the right channel really is separate. | Stage | Separate L/R? | Evidence | |---|---|---| | Android framework | Yes | `dumpsys media.audio_flinger`: speaker output is 2-channel FL/FR, *Master mono* off. The policy's speaker port is already stereo, so `stereoctl xml-patch` finds nothing to change. | | Dirac (Nothing's speaker tuning) | Not the fold | Session-0 insert effect, 2-in/2-out presets. Removing it alone changed nothing. | | MediaTek audio HAL (`audio.primary.mt6878.so`) | **Folds to mono** | `AudioALSAPlaybackHandlerBase::doStereoToMonoConversionIfNeed` writes (L+R)/2 to both channels whenever `MTK_AUDIO_NUMBER_OF_SPEAKER` is 1. Patching it out alone: still mono. | | Aurisys on the audio DSP, `smartpa_awinic` | **Folds to mono** | Awinic's speaker protection has one speaker model (`AW_DSP.bin`: five presets, each one 11,244-byte block for one speaker, all carrying 0.5/0.5 weights). With it replaced by MediaTek's pass-through `aurisys_demo` as well, the right slot went **silent** and the left slot still played. | | AFE routing | Yes | `I2SOUT4_CH2 <- DL_24CH_CH2` is live during playback. | | Awinic amp (`aw882xx`) | Yes | I2S slot select is register `0x06` bits 11:10 (`01` left, `10` right, `11` mono (L+R)/2), writable through the driver's `reg` attribute. Stock is left (`0x34e8`); on the right slot, cutting `I2SOUT4_CH2` silences the speaker. | | Earpiece | Left channel | `RCV <- ADDA_DL_CH1 <- DL_24CH_CH1`; `ADDA_DL_CH1` has no CH2 source. | A kernel never mattered: the routing, the amp driver, the HAL and the DSP libraries are all vendor code. Setting `MTK_AUDIO_NUMBER_OF_SPEAKER` to 2 was rejected: it also switches the HAL to a `dual_speaker_output` path that does not exist in this phone's `audio_device.xml`, and puts Awinic's protection into two-amp mode with one amp fitted. ### Protection: what Awinic does, and what stereo does Measured with CMF L/R Test DRIVER STUDY (tones from 100 Hz to 8 kHz at -30 to -3 dBFS; the HAL's and the DSP's own recordings of what reached them, and the HAL's raw 24-bit two-microphone capture): | | Awinic (mono, stock) | the module in stereo | |---|---|---| | Speaker peaks | about -5 dB below the amp's full output | about -6 dB (fixed attenuation); with boost, a limiter keeps them at -5 dB | | 100 Hz | cut by 16 dB at every level | untouched while quiet; held at -8 / -14 / -20 dB below full output when loud (light / medium / strong) | | 150 Hz-3 kHz | about +3.5 dB EQ | unchanged | | Earpiece | (not Awinic's) clips in its top 1.5 dB of full scale | limited at -2.5 dBFS; optional leveller raises quiet passages, peaks unchanged | Also measured: the speaker's resonance at about 1 kHz (from Awinic's current/voltage sense); Dirac (MUSIC) adds +5 to +6 dB at 200-500 Hz, a limiter at about -0.2 dBFS and a second harmonic on 100 Hz before either driver; the earpiece's whole path is at full level already (no hidden attenuation to win back). The limiters add at most 1.2 % distortion while working (50 Hz), under 0.1 % above 1 kHz; nothing changes while a signal is below its ceiling. ## Mono and stereo **Checksums**: every release lists the SHA-256 of its files, in the description and in `SHA256SUMS.txt`. **Test files**: every release carries `LEFT_ONLY_3min.wav` (left channel only) and `LEFT10s_RIGHT10s.wav` (spoken "left" / "right", then 10 s from that side only), built by `tools/make-test-audio.py`. In Stereo the left-only file plays from the earpiece alone, or the speaker alone when the phone is turned with the earpiece on your right; in Mono from both. ```sh stereoctl channels # what is running, and what is staged stereoctl channels stereo # switch to stereo now stereoctl channels mono # back to stock now ``` The CMF Stereo Manager app has the same switch, and so does the **Action** button on the module's card in Magisk (28 or newer), KernelSU and APatch: each press switches to the other mode and shows `stereoctl channels`' output. **Switching without a reboot** (v0.9.4). The module restarts the audio HAL (`setprop ctl.restart vendor.audio-hal`) on the wanted files instead of rebooting: about a second of silence, players pause, calls are unaffected (measured on the CMF Phone 1). Magisk bind-mounts each of the module's files over its vendor path at boot, in init's mount namespace, which the HAL shares (measured). A live switch takes those mounts of ours off (only ours: a mount from anywhere else on those paths and the switch is refused) and mounts what the wanted mode still needs: the staged files for stereo, nothing for mono, or, where Magisk left a placeholder rather than the stock file, a copy of the phone's own stock files (copied when it booted mono, or rebuilt from the stereo files by putting the original bytes back, and kept only when it hashes to the stock build). Every file is read back through `/proc/1/root` and must hash to the expected build; the new HAL process must still be running 3 s later. If any check fails, or a call is active, the mounts are undone and the change waits for a reboot. **What stereo changes**, and nothing else: 1. **The HAL fold**: `doStereoToMonoConversionIfNeed` no longer folds to mono; it loads the module's protection library and calls it for every buffer (`hal-swap/patch.S`), and the DSP task is told the speaker is stereo (`hw_info` bit `0x4`, two branches). Four places; the stock bytes every earlier version changed are written back first, and the result must hash to the tested build. 2. **The DSP fold**: `AURISYS_SCENARIO_DSP_PLAYBACK_SMARTPA` runs `aurisys_demo` instead of `smartpa_awinic`. The phone's own `aurisys_config_rv.xml` already declares `aurisys_demo` for that scenario (2 channels in/out, IV reference), so this is a configuration the vendor file provides. **Calls keep `smartpa_awinic`** (`DSP_CALL_FINAL` is untouched). 3. **The amp slot**: while the earpiece plays, the daemon puts the amp on the right slot; whenever the earpiece is not playing, on mono (L+R)/2, so the speaker never plays one channel alone. The driver resets the slot on every stream start, so the first second or two of a stream is the stock left slot until the daemon's next cycle. 4. **Attenuation**: the amp is held `STEREO_ATTEN_DB` (default 6 dB) down through its own volume control, `aw_dev_0_volume` (1/8 dB steps, per the aw882xx driver), less the speaker boost while the protection runs. Mono gives the amp its previous value back. 5. **Protection** (`protect/cmfstereo.c`, `stereoctl protect`): see [Protection](#protection-what-awinic-does-and-what-stereo-does) below. **No vendor file ships in this module** (the protection library is the module's own code). Staging copies this phone's own `audio.primary.mt6878.so`, `audio.primary.mediatek.so` and `aurisys_config_rv.xml`, checks their SHA-256 against the analysed build, patches them, and checks the result against the tested one before putting it in the module's overlay with the original SELinux labels. Anything else — another firmware, a different file — is refused and the phone stays on mono. After a Nothing OS update the hashes will differ and stereo will refuse until the new build has been checked. **Risks, plainly:** - Awinic's processing keeps the speaker within its excursion and temperature limits at high volume, from a live model of the speaker. In stereo, media gets the amp's hardware over-temperature / over-current cut-outs, the attenuation, and the module's fixed protection (peak and deep-bass limits measured against Awinic's, no temperature model). Use mono for loud listening, raise `STEREO_ATTEN_DB` if you play loud in stereo, and back off at the first distortion. - If the audio HAL restarts 3 times within a minute in stereo, the daemon puts the stock files back (mono) at once. - The earpiece has no protection in either mode (that was already true). - Two failed boots with the stereo overlay in place remove it and set `CHANNELS=mono` — the same watchdog the audio-policy overlay has. - With the daemon stopped (`stereoctl off`) the amp goes back to its stock left slot on the next stream, so in stereo the speaker would play the left channel alone. Switch to mono if you want the module off. - **Orientation**: turned with the earpiece on your right, Android itself swaps left and right before the audio HAL (the HAL's own recordings show the channels already swapped at rotation 270), except for a track whose session has its own audio effect chain (VLC's Dynamics Processing): that one reaches the HAL unswapped. The daemon finds such tracks in `dumpsys media.audio_flinger` (only while playing at rotation 270: when playback starts, when the phone turns, and every third 2 s cycle) and writes the output flags of their mixer threads to `vendor.audiohal.cmf_swap`; the HAL swaps a speaker stream only when the rotation (`vendor.audiohal.cmf_rotation`, stored by the HAL from Android's `rotation` parameter) is 270 and its output is named there. v0.9.5-v1.0.0 swapped by output, by Dirac tuning, then by patching the mixer; each rule held only for the apps it was tested with. MediaTek's "2nd loudspeaker" machinery **is** present on this build, in `/vendor/etc/audio_param/`: ``` 2nd Loudspeaker Compensation Filter (2nd-ACF) 2nd Loudspeaker High/Low Pass Filter Order bes_loudness_Sep_LR_Filter bes_loudness_L_* / bes_loudness_R_* (separate L and R filter sets) ``` An earlier revision of this file claimed it was absent. That was wrong — it came from the broken BRE greps fixed in the ERE commit, which reported a clean zero for a pattern that never matched anything. Whether the feature is merely MediaTek's stock parameter template or actually wired to a second transducer on this hardware is unresolved. --- ## Commands ``` stereoctl status module, daemon, and live control values stereoctl doctor diagnose why the earpiece is silent stereoctl reset clear saved state and start clean stereoctl probe [dir] dump the audio hardware stereoctl report fold the newest probe into one shareable .txt stereoctl on | off arm / disarm (off survives a reboot) stereoctl solo | unsolo speaker off, earpiece only - for auditioning stereoctl guard on | off re-enable / bypass the speaker-follows guard stereoctl apply | revert one-shot apply / restore stereoctl restart restart the watcher daemon stereoctl log [n] tail the log stereoctl scan [pattern] search the mixer for candidate controls stereoctl ctl NAME [VALUE] read or write one mixer control stereoctl dump every control and its value stereoctl diff [seconds] snapshot the mixer, wait, show what changed stereoctl channels [mono|stereo] show / choose the speaker channels (applied at once) stereoctl protect stereo protection: settings, and whether it runs stereoctl protect boost 0-6 speaker boost (dB less fixed attenuation, peaks still at Awinic's level; only while the protection runs) stereoctl protect bass off|light|medium|strong deep bass guard (below 100 Hz, only when loud) stereoctl protect earpiece on|off earpiece limiter (-2.5 dBFS) stereoctl protect leveller off|light|medium|strong earpiece leveller (quiet passages up 4 / 8 / 12 dB at most) stereoctl xml-patch install the stereo speaker-port overlay (reboot) stereoctl xml-revert remove it (reboot) ``` `stereoctl ctl` is the one to experiment with: find a candidate with `scan`, flip it while music plays, listen to the earpiece. --- ## Config Lives in `/data/adb/cmf-stereo/`, survives module updates. | file | what | |---|---| | `stereo.conf` | behaviour: mode, channels, attenuation, protection, poll interval, log level | | `actions.conf` | the routing itself, one action per line | | `stereo.log` | what the daemon did | | `state/` | saved original values, used to revert | `actions.conf` syntax: ``` ctl|| set an ALSA mixer control sysfs|| write to a sysfs node prop|| set a system property ``` `MODE=playback` (default) applies the routing only while something is playing. `MODE=always` keeps it on permanently — louder in theory, harder on the earpiece, and it costs idle power. `PLAYBACK_CTL` / `PLAYBACK_VALUE` decide how "audio is playing" is detected: one or more mixer controls separated by `|`, any of them reading the value means playing. Empty means scan `/proc/asound` for a RUNNING substream — which **misses DSP playback entirely**. On the CMF Phone 1 every kind of output has its own DSP task switch (measured, logged each second: a game turns on `dsp_fast_runtime_en`, a music player `dsp_music_runtime_en` with `dsp_primary_runtime_en`; `dsp_playback_runtime_en` stays on even when idle), so the installer sets all six playback tasks. Controls that cannot be read fall back to the procfs scan rather than reporting "never playing" forever. `SPEAKER_BOOST` (0-6, default 0), `BASS_PROTECT` (off / light / medium / strong, default medium), `EARPIECE_LIMIT` (on / off, default on) and `EARPIECE_LEVELLER` (off / light / medium / strong, default off) set the stereo protection; change them with `stereoctl protect` or the apps. `GUARD_CTL` / `GUARD_VALUE` gate the routing on a mixer control's value. On the CMF Phone 1 the guard is `aw_dev_0_switch` = `Enable`: the HAL disables the speaker amp when headphones or Bluetooth take over, so the earpiece follows the speaker instead of playing to nobody. One mixer read per cycle, no `dumpsys`. ### Earpiece gain, and how loud it can get `Handset Volume` is the receiver amp's gain on the MT6369 codec. Read from the codec driver (`snd-soc-mt6369.ko`): the control's range is 0–18, and the register runs the opposite way to the dB scale ALSA advertises for it: | value | gain | |---|---| | 0 | **+8 dB** (loudest) | | 8 | 0 dB | | 18 | −10 dB | | 31 | −40 dB (the codec's mute value) | Evidence: every output reads 31 at rest; the driver's put handler treats 31 as a special case; and the HAL itself sets 0 whenever it drives the receiver. **Versions before v0.9.2 shipped 31**, believing it was the top. That made the daemon pull the earpiece down to −40 dB every cycle while the HAL kept putting it back to +8 dB — the `Handset Volume: 0 -> 31` lines repeating in the log, and an earpiece that sounded weak and uneven. The installer now corrects any value above 18 to 0. The two earlier explanations in this README (that 31 was the ceiling, then that the control barely mattered) were both wrong; recorded rather than quietly edited, because the mistake is the useful part. `ADDA_DL_GAIN`, the digital gain before the DAC, is left alone: the HAL parks it at 63311 of 65535 (−0.3 dB), and `ADDA_DL` is shared with the headphone path. The earpiece is a receiver: it will not match the speaker, and it has no protection circuit. In stereo, balance the two by turning the **speaker** down (`STEREO_ATTEN_DB`), not by pushing the earpiece. ## Why it ships empty elsewhere The mixer control names are device-specific. A wrong write is, in ascending order of regret: nothing, silence, a HAL crash, or an earpiece driven past what a receiver is built for. The earpiece has a fraction of the excursion and power handling of the main speaker and there is no protection circuit assuming you will use it for music. So: probe first, then fill in real names. When you find a working route, start its gain low and raise it a step at a time. Distortion or rattle means back off — that damage does not come back. --- ## Safety and recovery **Boot watchdog.** If two consecutive boots fail to reach `sys.boot_completed` while the policy overlay is active, `post-fs-data.sh` deletes the overlay before it can be mounted again. A bad policy costs one extra reboot instead of a trip to recovery. **XML validation.** No patched policy is installed unless it passes a structural check — balanced ``, ``, `` and `` elements, intact root tag, no stray backslashes from a bad insertion. Android has no `xmllint`, and a malformed audio policy takes `audioserver` down hard enough to loop the boot. **Nothing OS updates.** An update replaces the vendor audio files the stereo overlay was patched from. Before anything is mounted at boot, `post-fs-data.sh` checks the vendor files against the analysed build; if they differ, the stereo overlay is removed and the phone boots on stock mono. The module's card and `stereoctl status` (`build: updated`) then say stereo is unavailable until a module release supports the new build. **Manual recovery**, if you ever need it: ```sh adb wait-for-device shell # or hold vol-down for safe mode su touch /data/adb/modules/cmf_stereo/disable reboot ``` Both Magisk and KernelSU honour the `disable` file, and `post-fs-data.sh` never touches audio when the actions list is empty. --- ## Credit: the Hi-Res Audio module This module owes a real debt to [**Hi-Res Audio™** by Adinata (@Adivenxnataly)](https://github.com/adivenxnataly/Hi-ResAudio). It is the reason we knew where to look. Before finding it, "use the earpiece as a second speaker on a MediaTek phone" was a vague idea with no entry point. That module is what pointed at MediaTek's `2nd Loudspeaker` / `bes_loudness` machinery and at the earpiece `` channel mask — and working out why those particular levers *don't* pan out on the CMF Phone 1 is what led to the routing that does. Reverse-engineering a vendor audio stack and giving the result away for free is generous work, and this project started from it. Thank you. It also aims at a different goal — high-resolution output, not dual speakers — so it is worth trying on its own terms if that is what you want. ### One bug worth reporting upstream Tested against `v2.0 with aaudio_mmap`, versionCode 20000, commit `78706f5` (2025-06-12). It bootlooped a CMF Phone 1, and the cause is a small typo with large consequences. In `customize.sh`: ```sh name="Apply Same Filter Setting with 2nd Loudspeaker\/> ``` The attribute value is never closed — `name="` opens a quote, then text, then `/>`, with no closing `"`. The fix is one character: ```sh name="Apply Same Filter Setting with 2nd Loudspeaker\"\/> ``` Without it, this reaches `Playback_ParamTreeView.xml`: ```xml

| 🔊 Stereo | Earpiece = left, speaker = right. Games, films and music finally have sides. |

| 📢 Mono | Default. Both speakers play the full mix: louder and fuller than the bottom speaker alone. |

| 📱 App | *CMF Stereo*, a clean Nothing-style app: on/off, Mono/Stereo, two 1–10 levels. |

| 🛟 Safe | Patches nothing it has not verified, never touches the vendor partition, and undoes itself after two failed boots. |

Install in three steps

  • Turn the phone sideways either way: left and right follow the screen.

    About

    A Magisk / KernelSU / APatch module that makes the CMF Phone 1 play media

    out of its earpiece as well as its bottom speaker — in true stereo if you

    want it.

    It has two channel modes:

  • **mono** (default, stock audio): both drivers play the same full mix —

    • louder, fuller and taller than the single bottom-firing speaker. This was

    the whole module once, back when it was called cmf-fake-stereo.

  • **stereo**: real left/right. The **earpiece plays the left channel and the

    • speaker the right**. It costs Awinic's speaker-protection processing on

    media; the module's own protection (a fixed amp attenuation, a deep bass

    guard and an earpiece limiter, measured against what Awinic does) stands in. See

    Mono and stereo.

    Getting stereo took finding the two places the phone folds the speaker to

    mono; the Findings section shows

    the measurements rather than asking you to take my word.

    Verified on A015 / Tetris, MT6878, Nothing OS B4.1, Android 16.

    What it does

  • **Real stereo** in stereo mode: earpiece = left channel, bottom speaker = right
  • **Mono** mode: both speakers play the full mix, with full speaker protection
  • Plays media through the earpiece alongside the speaker, automatically
  • Earpiece at the receiver amp's maximum, +8 dB (`Handset Volume 0`), the same value the HAL uses
  • Applies only while audio is playing, so the receiver is not held energised
  • Steps aside for headphones and Bluetooth
  • Restores every control it touches on stop, disarm or uninstall
  • Disarms itself if it ever causes a failed boot
  • Switch modes with `stereoctl channels mono|stereo`, the app, or the Action button on

    • the module's card in Magisk / KernelSU / APatch; the stereo overlay removes itself after

    two failed boots

  • Says on the module's card what is running: `[Stereo]`, `[Mono]`, `[Off]`, or

    • [Stereo unavailable] after a Nothing OS update

    What it does not do

  • **No Awinic protection on media in stereo.** Awinic's DSP processing is the

    • part that folds to mono, so stereo replaces it with the module's own, simpler

    protection (see Mono and stereo). Its model of the

    speaker, live from the amp's current and voltage sense, is not copied.

  • **No extra volume from the main speaker.** It is untouched.
  • **Nothing on other devices out of the box.** It installs inert elsewhere and

    • ships a probe to work out that device's routing.

    Quick start

    Flash the zip (build it with ./build.sh, or grab a release), reboot, play

    something. That is the whole setup on a CMF Phone 1 — the verified routing is

    preconfigured.

    To check it is working, with audio playing:

    su
stereoctl status     # all three controls should show want= matching now=
stereoctl solo       # speaker off, earpiece only - proves it is really the earpiece
stereoctl unsolo

    For real stereo (applied at once):

    su -c stereoctl channels stereo

    If it is ever silent, stereoctl doctor walks every layer that can cause that

    and names the one responsible.

    On other devices

    It installs with an empty actions.conf and changes nothing. Run

    stereoctl probe to dump the audio hardware — ALSA topology, every mixer

    control, smart-amp drivers, HAL configs and MediaTek's AudioParam tree — then

    stereoctl report to fold it into one shareable text file. The routing for

    that device gets written into actions.conf from what the probe finds. See

    Why it ships empty elsewhere.

    ---

    How it works

    Three layers, smallest hammer first.

    1. Mixer actions (actions.conf). The real work. An ALSA mixer control

    somewhere enables the receiver output stage; on MediaTek there is usually also

    a routing control that decides which DL (downlink) stream feeds it. Setting

    those while the speaker is playing is what puts the earpiece to work next to

    the speaker.

    The audio HAL rewrites mixer controls on every route change, so a one-shot

    write does not survive the next stream start. A small daemon re-asserts the

    values every couple of seconds and — by default — only while audio is actually

    playing, so the earpiece is not left energised all day.

    Everything touched has its original value saved under

    /data/adb/cmf-stereo/state/ and restored on stop, disarm or uninstall.

    2. Audio policy overlay (stereoctl xml-patch, optional). If the policy

    declares the speaker as AUDIO_CHANNEL_OUT_MONO, the framework downmixes to

    one channel before the HAL ever sees it, and no amount of mixer work brings

    the second channel back. The patch widens only the speaker to

    stereo, in an overlay copy — the vendor partition is never written. It is

    opt-in, validated before it is installed, and reversible.

    3. What the CMF Phone 1 actually needed. Worth recording, because it was

    not any of the obvious answers and the probe is what found it.

    Media on this device never touches the internal codec. Playback runs:

    DL_24CH_CH1/CH2 ──▶ I2SOUT4_CH1/CH2 ──▶ Awinic aw_dev_0 smart PA ──▶ speaker
                                  ◀── I2SIN4 ──▶ UL3   (IV-sense feedback)

    The earpiece hangs off the internal codec's DAC (ADDA_DL), and that DAC

    normally has no source connected at all — every one of its ~20 input

    switches sits Off. So pointing RCV Mux at the receiver routes it to a

    silent wire, which is exactly what happened on the first attempt.

    The switch that matters is ADDA_DL_CH1 DL_24CH_CH1: it feeds the internal

    DAC from the same DL_24CH stream already going to the speaker amp. Turn it

    on, then open RCV Mux, and the earpiece plays.

    There is only one Awinic device (aw_dev_0), so there is no second amp

    channel to press into service — the internal codec was the only way in.

    That alone gives both drivers the same full mix: mono mode. Real stereo

    needed one more step — switching off the two places the phone folds the

    speaker to mono — which is what stereoctl channels stereo adds (see

    Findings and

    Mono and stereo).

    Findings: what this device actually does

    Where the speaker is folded to mono

    Earlier revisions of this section said both transducers were hard-wired to

    channel 1, then that a custom kernel would be needed, then that the DSP

    firmware was the limit. All three were wrong. Each stage was measured with a

    test file that has sound on the left channel only and silence on the right,

    by switching the amp to its right slot: silence there means the right channel

    really is separate.

    | Stage | Separate L/R? | Evidence |

    |---|---|---|

    | Android framework | Yes | dumpsys media.audio_flinger: speaker output is 2-channel FL/FR, *Master mono* off. The policy's speaker port is already stereo, so stereoctl xml-patch finds nothing to change. |

    | Dirac (Nothing's speaker tuning) | Not the fold | Session-0 insert effect, 2-in/2-out presets. Removing it alone changed nothing. |

    | MediaTek audio HAL (audio.primary.mt6878.so) | Folds to mono | AudioALSAPlaybackHandlerBase::doStereoToMonoConversionIfNeed writes (L+R)/2 to both channels whenever MTK_AUDIO_NUMBER_OF_SPEAKER is 1. Patching it out alone: still mono. |

    | Aurisys on the audio DSP, smartpa_awinic | Folds to mono | Awinic's speaker protection has one speaker model (AW_DSP.bin: five presets, each one 11,244-byte block for one speaker, all carrying 0.5/0.5 weights). With it replaced by MediaTek's pass-through aurisys_demo as well, the right slot went silent and the left slot still played. |

    | AFE routing | Yes | I2SOUT4_CH2 <- DL_24CH_CH2 is live during playback. |

    | Awinic amp (aw882xx) | Yes | I2S slot select is register 0x06 bits 11:10 (01 left, 10 right, 11 mono (L+R)/2), writable through the driver's reg attribute. Stock is left (0x34e8); on the right slot, cutting I2SOUT4_CH2 silences the speaker. |

    | Earpiece | Left channel | RCV <- ADDA_DL_CH1 <- DL_24CH_CH1; ADDA_DL_CH1 has no CH2 source. |

    A kernel never mattered: the routing, the amp driver, the HAL and the DSP

    libraries are all vendor code. Setting MTK_AUDIO_NUMBER_OF_SPEAKER to 2 was

    rejected: it also switches the HAL to a dual_speaker_output path that does

    not exist in this phone's audio_device.xml, and puts Awinic's protection

    into two-amp mode with one amp fitted.

    Protection: what Awinic does, and what stereo does

    Measured with CMF L/R Test DRIVER STUDY (tones from 100 Hz to 8 kHz at -30 to -3 dBFS; the

    HAL's and the DSP's own recordings of what reached them, and the HAL's raw 24-bit two-microphone

    capture):

    | | Awinic (mono, stock) | the module in stereo |

    |---|---|---|

    | Speaker peaks | about -5 dB below the amp's full output | about -6 dB (fixed attenuation); with boost, a limiter keeps them at -5 dB |

    | 100 Hz | cut by 16 dB at every level | untouched while quiet; held at -8 / -14 / -20 dB below full output when loud (light / medium / strong) |

    | 150 Hz-3 kHz | about +3.5 dB EQ | unchanged |

    | Earpiece | (not Awinic's) clips in its top 1.5 dB of full scale | limited at -2.5 dBFS; optional leveller raises quiet passages, peaks unchanged |

    Also measured: the speaker's resonance at about 1 kHz (from Awinic's current/voltage sense);

    Dirac (MUSIC) adds +5 to +6 dB at 200-500 Hz, a limiter at about -0.2 dBFS and a second

    harmonic on 100 Hz before either driver; the earpiece's whole path is at full level already

    (no hidden attenuation to win back). The limiters add at most 1.2 % distortion while working

    (50 Hz), under 0.1 % above 1 kHz; nothing changes while a signal is below its ceiling.

    Mono and stereo

    Checksums: every release lists the SHA-256 of its files, in the description and in

    SHA256SUMS.txt.

    Test files: every release carries LEFT_ONLY_3min.wav (left channel only) and

    LEFT10s_RIGHT10s.wav (spoken "left" / "right", then 10 s from that side only), built by

    tools/make-test-audio.py. In Stereo the left-only file plays from the earpiece alone, or the

    speaker alone when the phone is turned with the earpiece on your right; in Mono from both.

    stereoctl channels            # what is running, and what is staged
stereoctl channels stereo     # switch to stereo now
stereoctl channels mono       # back to stock now

    The CMF Stereo Manager app has the same switch, and so does the Action button on the

    module's card in Magisk (28 or newer), KernelSU and APatch: each press switches to the

    other mode and shows stereoctl channels' output.

    Switching without a reboot (v0.9.4). The module restarts the audio HAL

    (setprop ctl.restart vendor.audio-hal) on the wanted files instead of

    rebooting: about a second of silence, players pause, calls are unaffected

    (measured on the CMF Phone 1). Magisk bind-mounts each of the module's files over its

    vendor path at boot, in init's mount namespace, which the HAL shares (measured).

    A live switch takes those mounts of ours off (only ours: a mount from anywhere

    else on those paths and the switch is refused) and mounts what the wanted mode

    still needs: the staged files for stereo, nothing for mono, or, where Magisk

    left a placeholder rather than the stock file, a copy of the phone's own stock

    files (copied when it booted mono, or rebuilt from the stereo files by putting

    the original bytes back, and kept only when it hashes to the stock build). Every

    file is read back through /proc/1/root and must hash to the expected build;

    the new HAL process must still be running 3 s later. If any check fails, or a

    call is active, the mounts are undone and the change waits for a reboot.

    What stereo changes, and nothing else:

  • **The HAL fold**: `doStereoToMonoConversionIfNeed` no longer folds to mono;

    • it loads the module's protection library and calls it for every buffer

    (hal-swap/patch.S), and the DSP task is told the speaker is stereo

    (hw_info bit 0x4, two branches). Four places; the stock bytes every

    earlier version changed are written back first, and the result must hash

    to the tested build.

  • **The DSP fold**: `AURISYS_SCENARIO_DSP_PLAYBACK_SMARTPA` runs

    • aurisys_demo instead of smartpa_awinic. The phone's own

    aurisys_config_rv.xml already declares aurisys_demo for that scenario

    (2 channels in/out, IV reference), so this is a configuration the vendor

    file provides. Calls keep smartpa_awinic (DSP_CALL_FINAL is

    untouched).

  • **The amp slot**: while the earpiece plays, the daemon puts the amp on the

    • right slot; whenever the earpiece is not playing, on mono (L+R)/2, so the

    speaker never plays one channel alone. The driver resets the slot on every

    stream start, so the first second or two of a stream is the stock left

    slot until the daemon's next cycle.

  • **Attenuation**: the amp is held `STEREO_ATTEN_DB` (default 6 dB) down

    • through its own volume control, aw_dev_0_volume (1/8 dB steps, per the

    aw882xx driver), less the speaker boost while the protection runs. Mono

    gives the amp its previous value back.

  • **Protection** (`protect/cmfstereo.c`, `stereoctl protect`): see

    • Protection below.

    No vendor file ships in this module (the protection library is the

    module's own code). Staging copies this phone's own

    audio.primary.mt6878.so, audio.primary.mediatek.so and

    aurisys_config_rv.xml, checks their SHA-256 against the analysed build,

    patches them, and checks the result against the tested one before putting it

    in the module's overlay with the original SELinux labels. Anything else —

    another firmware, a different file — is refused and the phone stays on mono.

    After a Nothing OS update the hashes will differ and stereo will refuse until

    the new build has been checked.

    Risks, plainly:

  • Awinic's processing keeps the speaker within its excursion and temperature

    • limits at high volume, from a live model of the speaker. In stereo, media gets

    the amp's hardware over-temperature / over-current cut-outs, the attenuation,

    and the module's fixed protection (peak and deep-bass limits measured against

    Awinic's, no temperature model). Use mono for loud listening, raise

    STEREO_ATTEN_DB if you play loud in stereo, and back off at the first

    distortion.

  • If the audio HAL restarts 3 times within a minute in stereo, the daemon puts

    • the stock files back (mono) at once.

  • The earpiece has no protection in either mode (that was already true).
  • Two failed boots with the stereo overlay in place remove it and set

    • CHANNELS=mono — the same watchdog the audio-policy overlay has.

  • With the daemon stopped (`stereoctl off`) the amp goes back to its stock

    • left slot on the next stream, so in stereo the speaker would play the left

    channel alone. Switch to mono if you want the module off.

  • **Orientation**: turned with the earpiece on your right, Android itself swaps left and

    • right before the audio HAL (the HAL's own recordings show the channels already swapped at

    rotation 270), except for a track whose session has its own audio effect chain (VLC's

    Dynamics Processing): that one reaches the HAL unswapped. The daemon finds such tracks in

    dumpsys media.audio_flinger (only while playing at rotation 270: when playback starts, when

    the phone turns, and every third 2 s cycle) and writes the output flags of their mixer

    threads to vendor.audiohal.cmf_swap; the HAL swaps a speaker stream only when the

    rotation (vendor.audiohal.cmf_rotation, stored by the HAL from Android's rotation

    parameter) is 270 and its output is named there. v0.9.5-v1.0.0 swapped by output, by Dirac

    tuning, then by patching the mixer; each rule held only for the apps it was tested with.

    MediaTek's "2nd loudspeaker" machinery is present on this build, in

    /vendor/etc/audio_param/:

    2nd Loudspeaker Compensation Filter (2nd-ACF)
2nd Loudspeaker High/Low Pass Filter Order
bes_loudness_Sep_LR_Filter
bes_loudness_L_*  /  bes_loudness_R_*   (separate L and R filter sets)

    An earlier revision of this file claimed it was absent. That was wrong — it

    came from the broken BRE greps fixed in the ERE commit, which reported a

    clean zero for a pattern that never matched anything. Whether the feature is

    merely MediaTek's stock parameter template or actually wired to a second

    transducer on this hardware is unresolved.

    Config

    Lives in /data/adb/cmf-stereo/, survives module updates.

    | file | what |

    |---|---|

    | stereo.conf | behaviour: mode, channels, attenuation, protection, poll interval, log level |

    | actions.conf | the routing itself, one action per line |

    | stereo.log | what the daemon did |

    | state/ | saved original values, used to revert |

    actions.conf syntax:

    ctl|<mixer control name>|<value>     set an ALSA mixer control
sysfs|<path>|<value>                 write to a sysfs node
prop|<property>|<value>              set a system property

    MODE=playback (default) applies the routing only while something is playing.

    MODE=always keeps it on permanently — louder in theory, harder on the

    earpiece, and it costs idle power.

    PLAYBACK_CTL / PLAYBACK_VALUE decide how "audio is playing" is detected:

    one or more mixer controls separated by |, any of them reading the value

    means playing. Empty means scan /proc/asound for a RUNNING substream — which

    misses DSP playback entirely. On the CMF Phone 1 every kind of output has

    its own DSP task switch (measured, logged each second: a game turns on

    dsp_fast_runtime_en, a music player dsp_music_runtime_en with

    dsp_primary_runtime_en; dsp_playback_runtime_en stays on even when idle),

    so the installer sets all six playback tasks. Controls that cannot be read

    fall back to the procfs scan rather than reporting "never playing" forever.

    SPEAKER_BOOST (0-6, default 0), BASS_PROTECT (off / light / medium /

    strong, default medium), EARPIECE_LIMIT (on / off, default on) and

    EARPIECE_LEVELLER (off / light / medium / strong, default off) set the stereo

    protection; change them with stereoctl protect or the apps.

    GUARD_CTL / GUARD_VALUE gate the routing on a mixer control's value. On

    the CMF Phone 1 the guard is aw_dev_0_switch = Enable: the HAL disables

    the speaker amp when headphones or Bluetooth take over, so the earpiece

    follows the speaker instead of playing to nobody. One mixer read per cycle,

    no dumpsys.

    Earpiece gain, and how loud it can get

    Handset Volume is the receiver amp's gain on the MT6369 codec. Read from the

    codec driver (snd-soc-mt6369.ko): the control's range is 0–18, and the

    register runs the opposite way to the dB scale ALSA advertises for it:

    | value | gain |

    |---|---|

    | 0 | +8 dB (loudest) |

    | 8 | 0 dB |

    | 18 | −10 dB |

    | 31 | −40 dB (the codec's mute value) |

    Evidence: every output reads 31 at rest; the driver's put handler treats 31

    as a special case; and the HAL itself sets 0 whenever it drives the receiver.

    Versions before v0.9.2 shipped 31, believing it was the top. That made

    the daemon pull the earpiece down to −40 dB every cycle while the HAL kept

    putting it back to +8 dB — the Handset Volume: 0 -> 31 lines repeating in

    the log, and an earpiece that sounded weak and uneven. The installer now

    corrects any value above 18 to 0. The two earlier explanations in this README

    (that 31 was the ceiling, then that the control barely mattered) were both

    wrong; recorded rather than quietly edited, because the mistake is the useful

    part.

    ADDA_DL_GAIN, the digital gain before the DAC, is left alone: the HAL parks

    it at 63311 of 65535 (−0.3 dB), and ADDA_DL is shared with the headphone

    path.

    The earpiece is a receiver: it will not match the speaker, and it has no

    protection circuit. In stereo, balance the two by turning the speaker down

    (STEREO_ATTEN_DB), not by pushing the earpiece.

    Why it ships empty elsewhere

    The mixer control names are device-specific. A wrong write is, in ascending

    order of regret: nothing, silence, a HAL crash, or an earpiece driven past

    what a receiver is built for. The earpiece has a fraction of the excursion and

    power handling of the main speaker and there is no protection circuit assuming

    you will use it for music.

    So: probe first, then fill in real names. When you find a working route, start

    its gain low and raise it a step at a time. Distortion or rattle means back

    off — that damage does not come back.

    ---

    Safety and recovery

    Boot watchdog. If two consecutive boots fail to reach sys.boot_completed

    while the policy overlay is active, post-fs-data.sh deletes the overlay

    before it can be mounted again. A bad policy costs one extra reboot instead of

    a trip to recovery.

    XML validation. No patched policy is installed unless it passes a

    structural check — balanced , , and

    elements, intact root tag, no stray backslashes from a bad

    insertion. Android has no xmllint, and a malformed audio policy takes

    audioserver down hard enough to loop the boot.

    Nothing OS updates. An update replaces the vendor audio files the stereo

    overlay was patched from. Before anything is mounted at boot, post-fs-data.sh

    checks the vendor files against the analysed build; if they differ, the stereo

    overlay is removed and the phone boots on stock mono. The module's card and

    stereoctl status (build: updated) then say stereo is unavailable until a

    module release supports the new build.

    Manual recovery, if you ever need it:

    adb wait-for-device shell           # or hold vol-down for safe mode
su
touch /data/adb/modules/cmf_stereo/disable
reboot

    Both Magisk and KernelSU honour the disable file, and post-fs-data.sh

    never touches audio when the actions list is empty.

    Credit: the Hi-Res Audio module

    This module owes a real debt to

    Hi-Res Audio™ by Adinata (@Adivenxnataly).

    It is the reason we knew where to look. Before finding it, "use the earpiece

    as a second speaker on a MediaTek phone" was a vague idea with no entry point.

    That module is what pointed at MediaTek's 2nd Loudspeaker / bes_loudness

    machinery and at the earpiece channel mask — and working out

    why those particular levers *don't* pan out on the CMF Phone 1 is what led to

    the routing that does. Reverse-engineering a vendor audio stack and giving the

    result away for free is generous work, and this project started from it.

    Thank you.

    It also aims at a different goal — high-resolution output, not dual speakers —

    so it is worth trying on its own terms if that is what you want.

    One bug worth reporting upstream

    Tested against v2.0 with aaudio_mmap, versionCode 20000, commit 78706f5

    (2025-06-12). It bootlooped a CMF Phone 1, and the cause is a small typo with

    large consequences. In customize.sh:

    name="Apply Same Filter Setting with 2nd Loudspeaker\/>

    The attribute value is never closed — name=" opens a quote, then text, then

    />, with no closing ". The fix is one character:

    name="Apply Same Filter Setting with 2nd Loudspeaker\"\/>

    Without it, this reaches Playback_ParamTreeView.xml:

    <Field ... name="Apply Same Filter Setting with 2nd Loudspeaker/>

    MediaTek's AudioParamParser cannot parse that, so the audio HAL aborts on

    every boot. The sed fires on any device carrying a bes_loudness_L_lpf_order

    field.

    Two other things to be aware of on a device like this one: it forces

    aaudio.mmap_policy=3 / aaudio.mmap_exclusive_policy=3 plus

    killall audioserver, which needs a HAL with an MMAP PCM path; and it sets

    the speaker channel mask to AUDIO_CHANNEL_OUT_SURROUND, which not every

    speaker port accepts.

    And a correction to an earlier version of this file, which claimed its

    insertions land mid-element: they do not. It computes the

    correct insertion point (POL + POLD - 1, the last line of the

    primary output block) and only writes when that matches a known constant,

    so placement is self-consistent, and otherwise it skips. That claim was wrong

    and is retracted.

    Why its stereo approach doesn't work on this device

    Not a criticism of the approach — it is sound on hardware that has a second

    loudspeaker. Two things stop it here (this module's stereo comes from a

    different route entirely, see Mono and stereo):

  • `Playback_ParamTreeView.xml` is the **view definition** for MediaTek's

    • parameter tuning tool (TreeRoot, Feature, FieldList,

    CategoryPathList). The runtime coefficients live in

    PlaybackACF_AudioParam.xml. Editing the view changes which fields a tuning

    application displays, not what the DSP does.

  • On the CMF Phone 1 every `bes_loudness_R_*` value and

    • bes_loudness_Sep_LR_Filter read 0x0 — MediaTek's stock template,

    untuned, because this phone has no second loudspeaker. And 2nd-ACF is a

    *filter* feature: it applies a different EQ curve to a second transducer's

    channel, it does not create a route to one.

    What this module took from it: edit the element you mean to change, validate

    the result, and keep a way back. Hence the block-aware awk, the XML

    structural check, and the boot watchdog.

    Do not run both modules at the same time — they touch the same files.

    ---

    tinymix

    Mixer controls cannot be read or written without a tinymix binary, and the

    CMF Phone 1 ships none. The module bundles one: a statically linked aarch64

    build of upstream tinyalsa, hardware backend only, no dlopen. Provenance,

    license and the exact build command are in bin/README.md.

    If you would rather not trust a shipped binary, build it yourself and drop it

    at /data/adb/cmf-stereo/bin/tinymix (chmod 0755) — that path is searched

    first. Termux's tinyalsa package works too.

    Search order: /data/adb/cmf-stereo/bin, the module's bin/, /vendor/bin,

    /system/bin, /odm/bin, /data/local/tmp, then $PATH. A vendor-supplied

    tinymix wins over the bundled one. Both the tinyalsa 1.x

    tinymix NAME VALUE and the 2.x tinymix set NAME VALUE calling conventions

    are handled, detected via --help rather than by guessing from an error

    message.

    ---

    Uninstall

    Remove it in your root manager. uninstall.sh stops the daemon and restores

    every control it touched. /data/adb/cmf-stereo/ is left in place so a

    reinstall does not lose your routing; delete it by hand for a clean slate.

    Development

    How a sound gets from an app to the two drivers (stereo)

    app -> Android's mixer (AudioFlinger)            swaps L/R itself at rotation 270,
                                                 except a track with its own effect
    -> Dirac (Nothing's tuning, session 0)
    -> audio HAL, AudioALSAPlaybackHandlerBase   patched: hal-swap/patch.S loads
       ::doStereoToMonoConversionIfNeed          protect/libcmfstereo.so and calls it
         rotation swap (VLC-type outputs)        <- vendor.audiohal.cmf_swap (daemon)
         speaker: bass guard, peak limiter       <- vendor.audiohal.cmf_*_ceil (daemon)
         earpiece: leveller, limiter
    -> audio DSP, aurisys_demo (pass-through)    aurisys_config_rv.xml patched
    -> DL_24CH ch1 -> codec DAC -> earpiece      routing: config/actions.cmf1.conf
       DL_24CH ch2 -> Awinic amp (right slot) -> speaker   amp slot/attenuation: daemon

    Measured end to end with the HAL's and the DSP's own recordings: nothing after the patched

    function changes the level, so the library's ceilings are exact.

    Files

    | path | what |

    |---|---|

    | customize.sh | install: device check, config kept across updates, stereo re-staged |

    | post-fs-data.sh | before Magisk mounts: boot watchdog, unknown-build guard |

    | service.sh | after boot: stock copies saved, the daemon started |

    | action.sh | Magisk's Action button: Mono <-> Stereo |

    | scripts/common.sh | config, logging, tinymix access, playback detection, the routing actions, the module card's text |

    | scripts/channels.sh | stereo: vendor file hashes and patches, staging, live switching, the amp, protection settings, crash-loop guard |

    | scripts/stereo-daemon.sh | keeps routing, amp slot, attenuation, rotation swap and protection applied while playing |

    | scripts/stereoctl | the CLI the apps and users call |

    | scripts/probe.sh | hardware dump |

    | scripts/xml_patch.sh | audio-policy overlay (opt-in, not for this device) |

    | hal-swap/ | the HAL patch in ARM64 assembly, and its emulator harness (run.sh) |

    | protect/ | the protection library (cmfstereo.c), its host tests and reproducible NDK build (build.sh) |

    | config/ | default settings and the verified CMF Phone 1 routing |

    | bin/tinymix | static aarch64 tinyalsa build, see bin/README.md |

    | tests/ | the off-device test suite and its recorded fixtures |

    | tools/make-test-audio.py | makes the left-only / left-right test files |

    Checks

    sh tests/run-tests.sh      # 194 checks; run under sh, dash, mksh and busybox sh
sh hal-swap/run.sh         # the HAL patch in qemu-aarch64 (needs clang, ld.lld, qemu)
sh protect/build.sh        # the library rebuilds byte for byte (needs the NDK)
./build.sh                 # the flashable zip

    Every vendor file is patched only after its hash proves it is the analysed build, and the

    result is hashed again; hal-swap/run.sh checks the bytes channels.sh writes against the

    assembled patch.
